description:
FOUND s494u (Opus, 2026-09-28) while building #2092 phase 1 (case mapping by regime).  perl 5.40.3 vs the s494u tree (scratch/s494u/qm.pl in the s494u worktree):

    sub hx { join " ", map { sprintf "%02X", ord } split //, $_[0] }
    print hx(quotemeta "\xC3\xA9"), "\n";          perl: 5C C3 5C A9     PCL: C3 5C A9
    print hx(quotemeta chr(0xE9)), "\n";           perl: 5C E9           PCL: E9
    { use feature 'unicode_strings'; print hx(quotemeta chr(0xE9)), "\n"; }   perl: E9   PCL: E9
    my $d = "\xC3\xA9"; utf8::decode($d); print hx(quotemeta $d), "\n";      perl: E9   PCL: E9
    print hx("\Q\xC3\xA9\E"), "\n";                perl: 5C C3 5C A9     PCL: C3 5C A9

perl's quotemeta is REGIME-dependent exactly like lc/uc (#2092): an unflagged string at a /d site has every char 128-255 escaped; a flagged one (or a unicode_strings site) uses the Unicode \w-ish rule PCL applies everywhere today (p-quotemeta: "escape unless Unicode alphanumeric").  Mostly harmless inside a regex (an unescaped high byte is still a literal) but VISIBLE when the result is printed or compared.
FIX SHAPE: the #2092 phase-1 machinery as built -- add p-quotemeta to ExprToCL's %CASE_MAP_OPS-style regime list (a :u operand at unicode_strings sites), a /d arm in the runtime that escapes every char >= 128 when %p-bytes-look-utf8-p says the string is bytes, and the compile-time twin in ExprToCL::_apply_mode's Q arm (it uses the transpiling perl's quotemeta today, which answers by the literal's accidental flag).  Error set = #2092's (a lone chr(0xE9) at /d is not bytes -> not escaped, perl escapes it).  Emission: :u at unicode_strings sites only (corpus-diff class = lc.t-like files).
BAR: the five rows above (row 2 = the documented sniff error), op/quotemeta.t + op/lc.t companion, corpus-diff one class, gen bump.
subject: quotemeta / \Q ignore the regime: at a /d site perl escapes EVERY high byte of an unflagged string (quotemeta "\xC3\xA9" = \\\xC3\\\xA9), PCL leaves \xC3 bare -- the #2092 phase-1 mechanism (regime operand + sniff) applies
